Because people asked for it here is a discussion of the pre-war ear from a Japanese perspective. I also learned there is a limit on the size of a VOAT post - who knew?! This is part 1 of 2.

This is a hopefully interesting account of how the Japanese ended up becoming involved in WW II. As a story it has all the elements of great fiction. Unfortunately for many it is all true.

Most people know that from the mid 15th century, basically the dawn of worldwide European exploration, Japan had been isolationists. There was some minimal diplomatic relations but no immigration or emigration or trade.

OPENING THE GATES

This all changed when US Navy Commodore Perry steamed into Tokyo Bay on 7/8/1853. Although no exact record of what was said survives this supreme diplomat, because all US Navy warship commanders are know first for diplomacy, presented the Japanese with a paradoxical choice. Open full trade with America or open war. The nominally medieval Japanese seemed particularly impressed with his Paixhans Guns. Paixhans were one of the first modern artillery guns designed specifically to fire exploding shells instead of inert “balls”.

So peaceful trade, literally at the point of a gun, was opened.

The Japanese enthusiastically embraced technology. Likely in no small part from being brought out of self imposed isolation at the point of a gun. Less than 10 years later the first domestic steam engine production was beginning.

It is important to note that the Japanese were seldom a peaceful people. Their weapons and tactics were stuck firmly in 13th century Europe, both long before and long after Europe itself passed through that stage. Adding steam and gunpowder improved efficiency more than changed the culture.

Thus Japan had a natural talent for warfare. And as it turns out industrialization. As most people are aware standardized testing shows Japanese to be among the most intelligent group of people on earth.

RUSSO-JAPANESE WAR

Still most of the world was surprised when the Russians were thoroughly trounced by the Japanese in the Russo-Japanese war (1904-1905). This is an absolutely pivotal event! This war established Japanese control beyond the home islands.

Japan would soon learn the lesson of the victor. Once which history classes never mention. Now you own this defeated people and all the infrastructure you just spent a fortune destroying. Similarly the great de-colonization push following WWII was much more about the exhausted, and bankrupt, nations of Europe simply no longer being able to afford the expense of dragging recalcitrant Africans out of the stone age. Colonization on earth is now dead because there is nothing of value to colonize any more. Even in America with its “colonies” (legally possessions) of Guam, US Virgin Islands, and Puerto Rico, they are a net sink. Especially Puerto Rico. A dollar gobbling black hole on the national budget that can never be filled.

But back to Japan on the Asian mainland. Following the Treaty of Portsmouth Japan now more or less owned Manchuria and annexed Korea to the outrage of exactly no one. Neither Russia, the US, nor anyone else really cared exactly where Japan drew the lines on their new possessions.

Unfortunately as Mr. Spock so famously observed: Wanting can be a much more desirable thing than having. It is not logical. But it is often true.

Japan soon met opposition from multiple Chinese factions. As it transpired, and this is another KEY POINT in history, Chinese nationalists wanted the Japanese out. The Chinese communists, the second most powerful faction were quite happy to sit back and wait until everyone was exhausted. Then they would come in the night like the cowards communists have always been.

In practice this meant that by the late 1920s Japan was fully involved in military operations that clearer minds could see they would never win. They simply lacked the manpower for a war of attrition. But the Japanese also had powerful and important allies that saw Japan as the lesser of the many evils facing every side of China.

Now in classic, or perhaps bad, novel form comes the False Flag: The Manchurian Incident.

THE MANCHURIAN INCIDENT

Frustrated by Japanese “nation building” a group of mid level Japanese Army officers conspired in plan to commit treason against Japan, kill a significant number of important allies and loyal Japanese officers. In a country that defines itself on honor this could be argued to be one of the most disgraceful incidents in all Japanese history.

The bombing was carried out by these conspirators and evidence planted to implicate Japanese allies in China. Outraged by the betrayal Japanese high command began a scorched earth war in China. The date was 1931. We are still 10 years away from Perl Harbor. But an entirely new direction has been set.

In the ensuing battles Chinese Communists conducted harassing actions against Chinese Nationalists but carefully avoided engaging the overwhelming Japanese Army. Predictably the Japanese then saw the communists as an annoyance that would eventually require attention but the Nationalists were the opponent now in the war. The other factions faded into military insignificance.

Japan had nothing remotely approaching the resources needed to subdue China. They compensated by becoming ever more brutal. Terrorizing civilians and conducted HUNDREDS of poison gas attacks. Although poison gas has seldom proven the effective battle weapon armchair generals want it to be, it is a terror weapon par-excellence.

We need to add that Japan’s actions all the while were being encouraged by their US progenitors. Much hay was made by US leaders whispering in Japanese ears about “Japanese Manifest Destiny”.

WAR IN EUROPE

The breathtakingly evil Treaty of Versailles ensured another continent wide war in Europe. So no one schooled in cause and effect was too surprised when less than 20 years after WW I Europe was - at it again.

The US involvement in WW I had profoundly different effects on government elite vs the American population. Millions of Americans died, millions more permanently maimed in what most Americans saw as a pointless action. While President Wilson went to great lengths to cover the fact, the sinking of the Lusitania was in fact a valid military action because the US had been smuggling munitions to England for years. Far from the neutral country claimed the US had probably already lengthened the war.

By 1917 when the US came roaring onto the scene with millions of fresh faced boys ready to die for the honor of Arch Duke Ferdinand Russia had just quit - probably the only case in history of a major combatant in a war taking their ball and going home. All other parties were beyond bankrupt. Destitute with bills that are not paid off 100 years later is more accurate. Without US intervention all parties would have sued for honorable peace and Europe, not to mention the 20th century would have been a very different animal. Coming along in all of this was Japan. A close US ally it was natural for them to join the war effort. Although they served no significant part in the fighting there was no doubt great national pride in being on the winning side of a World War.

Fast forward 20 years and a new war is raging in Europe where a miraculously rebuilt Germany is on the verge of conquering the entire European continent.

Americans back then still remembered the adage: Fool me once shame on you, fool me twice shame on me. Everyone who was anyone was violently opposed to another war in Europe. This most notably included most all the voters. Henry Ford himself was one of the most vocal opponents going so far as to wonder: If American does get involved on which side should we fight?

On the other side of the world Japan continued to prove that if you kill 1000 Chinese they will be replaced tomorrow with 1500. The Emperor was furious with the Prime Minister who had assured him a decade earlier following the Manchurian Incident that Chinese opposition to Japanese rule could be crushed in a year.

FDR NEEDS A FALSE FLAG

For FDR it was obvious by 1939 that Americans didn’t give a fresh damn where the borders on Europe’s map were drawn or which petty tyrant called himself the leader. Even the siege of England failed to get anyone’s attention.

So FDR began arming China, even sending US mercenaries to fly US aircraft against Japan. But that wasn’t enough by half. First since this was a covert action he couldn’t very well say on his radio address that the Japanese were killing American pilots in China. The national outrage would be “What the HELL are American pilots doing in China”!

If Americans were unmoved by German Area bombing of downtown London, sinking another munitions ship wasn’t going to work either.

So, FDR decided to burn one of America’s closest and most reliable allies. A country that marched in lock step with the American agenda for its entire 80 years of on the world stage: Japan.

Japan is uniquely resource poor in the raw materials that make industrialization go. Remarkably stoic in the face of adversity the Japanese used Hashima Island: little more than a high spot in the Pacific Ocean, 9 miles off the cost of Nagasaki as one of the main sources of coal for the entire country. To call the working conditions inhuman would be generous. But that is where the coal was so that is where the Japanese were.

But coal doesn’t work as an aircraft fuel. It also doesn’t make steel without iron. So FDR had his wedge. He switched from tactile support of Japan in China, which not 1 in 1000 Americans knew where China was or that Japan had troops there. Now Japan was an evil invader against the Chinese nationalists - best not to mention those communists waiting in the wings.
